title: DEPUTYBENCH: Evaluating Contextual Safety in Enterprise Agents
abstract: arXiv:2611.13355v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Enterprise agents must determine whether ordinary requests are permitted by organizational records and policies while continuing legitimate work. We introduce DEPUTYBENCH, an executable benchmark with 79 base items, 375 instances, paired permission contexts, and graded evidence requirements. Across 12 models, revised audits give 88.0% pooled safety and 79.1% paired success. A controlled study of 28 derived tasks and six models tests authorization-fact flips, evidence masking, and irrelevant rewrites. Outcomes track backend permissions, yet restricted execution is more frequent with missing evidence than explicit non-permission: 10.3% versus 3.5% on 27 matched tasks, a 6.8-percentage-point difference (95% interval: 1.9-13.0; secondary analysis). translated_title: DEPUTYBENCH：评估企业智能体的情境安全性
translated_abstract: 企业智能体必须在继续开展合法工作的同时，判断普通请求是否被组织记录与政策所允许。我们提出了DEPUTYBENCH，这是一个可执行的基准测试，包含79个基础条目、375个实例、成对的权限上下文以及分级的证据要求。在12个模型上，修订后的审计得到了88.0%的总体安全性和79.1%的成对成功率。一项针对28个衍生任务和6个模型的受控研究测试了授权事实翻转、证据遮蔽和不相关改写。实验结果总体上遵循后端权限，然而与明确的不许可相比，证据缺失时受限执行更为频繁：在27个匹配任务上分别为10.3%对3.5%，相差6.8个百分点（95%区间：1.9-13.0；次要分析）。事后分析发现，100次遮蔽条件下的执行中有61次发生在四个需要完整累计计数或特定个人同意的隐私任务中。当错误最……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出了可执行基准DEPUTYBENCH来评估企业智能体在组织权限与证据约束下的情境安全性，并揭示了一个关键风险：模型在证据缺失时比在明确禁止时更容易越权执行受限操作（10.3%对3.5%）。
en_tdlr: DEPUTYBENCH is an executable benchmark for evaluating contextual safety in enterprise agents under organizational permissions, revealing that models execute restricted actions more often when evidence is missing than when explicitly prohibited (10.3% vs 3.5%).
